name: 34th Street (Harvest34)
headline: Boulder Housing Partners, the City of Boulder's housing authority, plans Harvest34, 44 all-electric, townhouse-style rental homes for households at 40% and 60% AMI, with a community center, on a 4.5-acre site it land-banked in 2015 at 3125 34th Street in north Boulder. It won a 2025 federal 4% award with state and TOC credit from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It is a small, low-density family deal carried by a housing authority's own land bank, city money and banked bond cap; CHFA lists Longmont Housing Authority as bond issuer even though BHP's board induced the bonds itself, and as of mid-2026 the project was still in city permitting.

status.label: Credits awarded; in city permitting, construction start not confirmed
status.detail: Boulder Housing Partners' project page (updated 2026-06-17) says Harvest34 is in the permitting process with the City of Boulder and construction is expected to start later in 2026. No public record of a financial closing, building permit or groundbreaking was found.

next_step: Watch for a Boulder building permit, a bond issuance resolution (Longmont Housing Authority or BHP) and a closing or groundbreaking notice from BHP.

key_numbers.meaning: 10 one-bedroom, 24 two-bedroom and 10 three-bedroom homes; 6 at 40% AMI and 38 at 60% AMI.
Plus $440,000 noncompetitive state credit and $57,200 TOC credit.
CHFA lists Longmont Housing Authority as issuer; BHP's board had induced up to $20,000,000 of its own bonds in 2024.
Affordable Housing Fund award announced 2025-11-26, on top of $3,000,000 in city money used to buy the land in 2015.

facts.value: Family, new construction; cycle year 2025; QCT yes, DDA no; no Section 8
4.5-acre vacant lot east of the Orchard Grove Mobile Home Park; formerly known as the Orchard Grove Project; the name Harvest34 refers to the site's history as an orchard

44 townhouse-style (single-family-style) rental homes, a net-zero community center, playground, community and pollinator gardens and walking paths; all-electric; keeps a wildlife corridor and open space along the community ditch
By-right under current zoning; Site Review went to city planning staff, with Planning Board only if called up

BHP planned to use CHFA cap and cap it already held; it held $31,733,410 of banked cap in September 2024, including $6,647,089 of 2024 City of Boulder cap carried forward for projects including 34th Street

background.text: BHP bought the vacant 4.5-acre lot in 2015 with $3,000,000 of city money and $450,000 of its own to land-bank it for affordable housing, and began planning in 2017.

After several site layouts, BHP settled on 44 townhome-style units, a community center, playground and community garden, built to current zoning and shaped by community input. A community meeting in May 2024 was mostly supportive, per board minutes.

BHP's board adopted Inducement Resolution #2024-5 on 2024-07-10, declaring intent to issue up to $20,000,000 of multifamily housing revenue bonds and allowing reimbursement of pre-closing costs by the future LIHTC partnership.

In July 2024 BHP planned to apply on 2024-08-01 for 4% federal credits, state credits and bonds, close and start construction in late 2025. The award came in the 2025 cycle and the start slipped to 2026.
BHP's 2024 annual report lists 3125 34th St (44 units) among entitlements completed in 2024.
On 2024-09-11 BHP's board carried forward $6,647,089 of 2024 City of Boulder bond cap for future projects including 34th Street (Resolution #2024-8).
The city calls the homes permanently affordable.

timeline.event: BHP buys the 4.5-acre site with city support
BHP board adopts Inducement Resolution #2024-5 (up to $20M of bonds); Site Review is with city staff
BHP board carries forward 2024 bond cap for projects including 34th Street (Resolution #2024-8)
Entitlements completed, per BHP's 2024 annual report
City of Boulder announces a $4,400,000 Affordable Housing Fund award
BHP project page says Harvest34 is in permitting, with construction expected later in 2026
Listed under cycle year 2025 on CHFA's Federal 4% award report

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report names Longmont Housing Authority as the bond issuer, while BHP's 2024 inducement resolution declared BHP's own intent to issue the bonds.
The City of Boulder says the homes will serve households at 30% to 60% AMI, while CHFA's award report lists 6 units at 40% AMI and 38 at 60% AMI, with none at 30%.
BHP's July 2024 board memo describes 44 apartment homes in townhome-style units, while its current project page describes 44 single-family-style rental homes and the city says townhouse-style homes.
